medications.startingDose: 10 mg once daily (5 mg in elderly or sensitive anxiety patients)
medications.titration: Increase by 5-10 mg after minimum 1-2 weeks as tolerated
medications.maxCeiling: 20 mg/day (10 mg/day in elderly or CYP2C19 poor metabolizers due to QTc risk)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2C19 (primary), CYP3A4, CYP2D6. Minimal CYP enzyme inhibition (clean drug interaction profile).
monitoring: QTc if combined with other QTc-prolonging agents or high dose
medications.clinicalPearls: Often considered the most selective SSRI with minimal drug-drug interactions. Very clean starting agent for mixed depression/anxiety.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (<25 years).

medications.startingDose: 25 - 50 mg once daily (morning or evening)
medications.titration: Increase by 25 - 50 mg every 1 - 2 weeks based on response
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP3A4. Mild CYP2D6 inhibitor at higher doses (>100mg).
medications.clinicalPearls: First-line preferred in cardiac patients (SADHART trial). Take with a full meal to reduce nausea. Mild dopamine reuptake at high doses.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 10 - 20 mg once daily in morning
medications.titration: Increase by 10 - 20 mg after 2 - 4 weeks (slow accumulation)
medications.halfLife: Parent drug: 2 - 4 days; Norfluoxetine: 7 - 15 days (built-in self-taper)
medications.cypMetabolism: Strong inhibitor of CYP2D6 and CYP2C19. Substrate of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Drug interactions (Tamoxifen, beta-blockers, TCAs due to 2D6)
medications.clinicalPearls: Energizing/activating profile; excellent for fatigued, lethargic depression. Long half-life minimizes withdrawal/discontinuation syndrome if doses are missed.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 150 mg once daily in morning
medications.titration: Increase to 300 mg once daily after 4-7 days if tolerated
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2B6 substrate. Strong inhibitor of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Eating disorder history (absolute contraindication: seizure risk)
medications.clinicalPearls: Zero sexual side effects; weight neutral or promotes weight loss. Great for depression with sluggishness, low motivation, or comorbid ADHD. Dose in morning to avoid insomnia.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Contraindicated in patients with seizure history, bulimia, or anorexia nervosa due to lowered seizure threshold.

medications.startingDose: 30 mg once daily for 1 week, then 60 mg once daily
medications.titration: Increase to 60 mg daily; doses >60 mg offer little added antidepressant efficacy but increase side effects
medications.cypMetabolism: Substrate of CYP1A2, CYP2D6. Moderate inhibitor of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Hepatic function (avoid in chronic liver disease or heavy alcohol use)
medications.clinicalPearls: Dual-action first-line choice when depression or anxiety is accompanied by chronic somatic pain, fibromyalgia, or neuropathic symptoms.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 37.5 mg - 75 mg once daily with food
medications.titration: Increase by 37.5 - 75 mg every 1-2 weeks as tolerated
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 substrate to active metabolite (Desvenlafaxine).
medications.clinicalPearls: Acts almost purely as an SSRI below 150 mg; dual norepinephrine reuptake kicks in at 150 mg and above. Must cross-taper slowly to avoid electric shock sensations (brain zaps).
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 7.5 - 15 mg once daily at bedtime
medications.titration: Increase by 15 mg every 1-2 weeks up to 45 mg
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP1A2, CYP2D6, CYP3A4 substrate.
monitoring: CBC if signs of infection (rare agranulocytosis)
medications.clinicalPearls: Paradoxical dosing: Lower doses (7.5-15mg) are heavily antihistaminic (sedation/appetite); higher doses (30-45mg) increase noradrenergic transmission, becoming less sedating. Great adjunct for insomnia/underweight patients.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

indications: Moderate to Severe Binge Eating Disorder (Adults)
medications.startingDose: 20 - 30 mg once daily in morning
medications.titration: Increase by 10 - 20 mg weekly intervals
medications.halfLife: Prodrug cleaved in RBCs; d-amphetamine half-life ~10-12 hours (smooth 12-14 hr clinical coverage)
medications.cypMetabolism: Not dependent on CYP450 for activation (enzymatic hydrolysis in red blood cells).
monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate at each follow-up
WA State PDMP check prior to each refill
medications.clinicalPearls: Prodrug design resists crushing/snorting/inhalation, reducing abuse liability compared to immediate-release stimulants. Very consistent, non-jittery pharmacokinetic curve.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Schedule II controlled substance: High potential for abuse and dependence. Monitor cardiovascular status.

medications.startingDose: 10 - 20 mg once daily in morning
medications.titration: Increase by 5 - 10 mg weekly
medications.halfLife: d-amphetamine ~10 hrs; l-amphetamine ~13 hrs (Dual-bead delivery gives 8-10 hrs effect)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 substrate; gastrointestinal pH affects absorption.
medications.clinicalPearls: Contains 75% dextroamphetamine and 25% levoamphetamine. The levo-isomer provides peripheral stimulation which some patients perceive as improved physical motivation, but others find anxiety-provoking.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Schedule II controlled substance: High potential for abuse and cardiovascular risk.

medications.startingDose: 40 mg once daily (or 20 mg BID)
medications.titration: Increase after minimum 3-7 days to target 80 mg/day
medications.halfLife: 5 hours in extensive metabolizers (up to 24 hrs in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 substrate (dramatic exposure difference based on 2D6 genetics or strong 2D6 inhibitors like fluoxetine/bupropion).
monitoring: Liver enzymes if jaundice or symptoms appear
medications.clinicalPearls: Non-controlled alternative for ADHD when stimulants are contraindicated (substance use disorder history, severe anxiety, tic disorder, or cardiac risk). Takes 4-6 weeks for full therapeutic effect (unlike stimulants which work day 1).
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal ideation in children and adolescents.

medications.startingDose: 7.5 mg twice daily (15 mg/day total)
medications.titration: Increase by 5 mg/day every 2-3 days as needed
medications.therapeuticRange: 20 - 40 mg/day in divided doses (BID or TID)
medications.halfLife: 2 - 3 hours (requires scheduled BID or TID administration)
medications.cypMetabolism: Extensively metabolized by CYP3A4. Grapefruit juice significantly increases levels.
medications.clinicalPearls: Non-sedating, non-addictive, non-controlled anxiolytic. Does NOT work PRN like a benzodiazepine; must be taken daily on a scheduled basis. Excellent adjunct to an SSRI for residual anxiety or to mitigate SSRI sexual side effects.
medications.blackBoxWarning: None.

medications.startingDose: 25 mg daily for Weeks 1 and 2
medications.titration: MANDATORY SLOW TITRATION: 50 mg daily for Weeks 3 and 4; 100 mg daily for Week 5; 200 mg daily for Week 6+
medications.cypMetabolism: Glucuronidation (UGT1A4). Valproate doubles lamotrigine levels (cut dose in half). Carbamazepine/OCPs cut levels in half.
monitoring: Immediate skin inspection for rash, fever, mucosal involvement
Must re-titrate from 25mg if missed for >5 half-lives (>4-5 days)
medications.clinicalPearls: The premier mood stabilizer for bipolar depression (unlike lithium which is stronger for mania). Highly weight neutral with no cognitive dulling. Crucial rule: Never titrate fast.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Serious, life-threatening skin rashes including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Rate of rash is highest with rapid titration.

medications.startingDose: 2 - 5 mg once daily (morning preferred to prevent insomnia)
medications.titration: For MDD augmentation: titrate slowly by 2-5 mg every 1-2 weeks. Target dose for MDD is typically 2-10 mg/day.
medications.therapeuticRange: MDD Adjunct: 2 - 10 mg/day; Bipolar Mania/Schizophrenia: 15 - 30 mg/day
medications.halfLife: 75 hours (active dehydro-aripiprazole: 94 hours; takes ~2 weeks to reach steady state)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 substrate. Reduce dose by 50% if co-administered with strong 2D6 inhibitors (bupropion, fluoxetine) or 3A4 inhibitors.
monitoring: AIMS exam baseline and every 6-12 months
Fasting blood glucose/HbA1c and lipid panel baseline, 3 months, then annually
medications.clinicalPearls: D2 partial agonist ('dopamine stabilizer'): boosts dopamine in hypo-dopaminergic pathways (prefrontal cortex) while blocking in hyper-dopaminergic pathways. Very low metabolic/weight gain risk compared to Olanzapine/Quetiapine, and zero prolactin elevation. Watch closely for akathisia—patients often mistake physical inner restlessness for worsening anxiety; treat with propranolol if needed.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: Bipolar Depression: 50 mg at bedtime (Day 1), 100 mg (Day 2), 200 mg (Day 3), 300 mg (Day 4); MDD Adjunct XR: 50 mg at bedtime
medications.titration: MDD Adjunct: Increase to 150-300 mg at bedtime over 1-2 weeks; Bipolar Depression target: 300 mg at bedtime
medications.therapeuticRange: MDD Adjunct: 150 - 300 mg/day; Bipolar Depression: 300 mg/day; Mania/Psychosis: 400 - 800 mg/day
medications.halfLife: Quetiapine: 6 hours; Active metabolite Norquetiapine: 12 hours
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP3A4 primary substrate. Co-administration with strong 3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) requires 1/6th dose reduction.
monitoring: Fasting blood glucose/HbA1c & fasting lipid panel baseline, 3 mos, then annually
medications.clinicalPearls: Dose-dependent receptor pharmacology: At 50mg, primarily H1 antihistamine (pure sedation/sleep); at 150-300mg, active norquetiapine NET inhibition + 5HT2A antagonism produces antidepressant effect; at 400-800mg, D2 receptor occupancy reaches 65%+ producing antipsychotic/antimanic effects. One of only four FDA-approved monotherapies for bipolar depression.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Suicidal ideation warning in patients <25 years.

indications: Bipolar I Depression (Monotherapy or Adjunct to Lithium/Valproate)
medications.startingDose: 20 - 40 mg once daily with an evening meal
medications.titration: Increase by 20 - 40 mg after 1-2 weeks based on clinical response
medications.therapeuticRange: Bipolar Depression: 20 - 60 mg/day (doses >60mg rarely add efficacy for bipolar depression); Schizophrenia: 40 - 120 mg/day
medications.maxCeiling: 120 mg/day (Bipolar Depression max 120mg, though 20-60mg is standard target)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP3A4 primary substrate. Absolute contraindication with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ketoconazole) or inducers (carbamazepine, St. John's wort).
monitoring: Baseline and annual metabolic labs (fasting glucose, lipids)
medications.clinicalPearls: MANDATORY FOOD RULE: Must be taken with a substantial meal containing at least 350 calories (preferably healthy fats) to ensure adequate bioavailability; taking without food cuts absorption by 50%! Highly favorable metabolic and cardiac profile (near zero weight gain, no QTc prolongation). Category B in pregnancy historical registry.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Suicidality warning in young adults <25.

medications.class: Serotonin Antagonist and Reuptake Inhibitor (SARI / Hypnotic)
medications.startingDose: Insomnia: 25 - 50 mg at bedtime; MDD: 150 mg/day in divided doses
medications.titration: Insomnia: Increase to 50 - 100 mg (up to 150 mg) at bedtime after 3-5 days as needed
medications.therapeuticRange: Insomnia: 25 - 100 mg at bedtime; Antidepressant: 150 - 400 mg/day (rarely used for MDD due to excessive daytime somnolence)
medications.maxCeiling: 150 - 200 mg at bedtime for insomnia; 400 mg/day outpatient for depression
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP3A4 primary substrate to active metabolite mCPP.
monitoring: Advise male patients regarding emergency ER protocol for sustained painful erection (>4 hrs)
medications.clinicalPearls: Non-controlled, non-habit-forming sleep architecture stabilizer. Does NOT alter normal REM/slow-wave sleep architecture unlike benzodiazepines or Z-drugs (Ambien). Doses of 25-50mg saturate 5-HT2A, H1, and alpha-1 receptors, causing sleep induction without stimulating 5-HT reuptake.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 25 - 50 mg PO PRN every 6-8 hours as needed for acute anxiety or panic symptoms
medications.titration: Titrate by 25 mg increments based on tolerability and daytime sedation
medications.therapeuticRange: 25 - 50 mg PO BID-TID PRN (or 50-100 mg at bedtime for acute insomnia)
medications.maxCeiling: 100 mg/day (max 50 mg/day in elderly or hepatic impairment)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6, CYP3A4/5, alcohol dehydrogenase. Active metabolite is cetirizine (Zyrtec).
monitoring: Cardiac QTc prolongation warning: Avoid combining with other QTc-prolonging drugs (citalopram, ondansetron)
medications.clinicalPearls: Premier non-controlled, non-scheduled alternative to benzodiazepines (Xanax/Ativan) for acute panic surges and somatic anxiety. Onset of action is 15-30 minutes. Hydroxyzine pamoate (Vistaril) is more lipophilic and preferred for anxiety over hydroxyzine hydrochloride (Atarax).
medications.blackBoxWarning: None.

medications.class: Selective Alpha-2A Adrenergic Receptor Agonist (Non-Stimulant, Non-Controlled)
medications.startingDose: 1 mg once daily in the evening or morning
medications.titration: Increase by 1 mg weekly based on response and tolerability
medications.maxCeiling: 4 mg/day (rarely 7mg based on weight in adolescent guidelines)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP3A4/5 substrate.
monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate baseline, dose changes, and periodically
NEVER discontinue abruptly: rebound hypertension risk
medications.clinicalPearls: 15-20 times more selective for alpha-2A receptors than clonidine, causing significantly less sedation and hypotension. Enhances prefrontal cortical connectivity and working memory. Outstanding adjunct to smooth out stimulant irritability or treat comorbid emotional dysregulation/rejection sensitive dysphoria.
medications.blackBoxWarning: None.

medications.startingDose: Performance Anxiety: 10 - 20 mg PO 30-60 minutes prior to anxiety trigger; Akathisia: 10 - 20 mg BID-TID
medications.titration: Increase by 10-20 mg as tolerated, up to 40-80 mg/day for akathisia
medications.therapeuticRange: 10 - 40 mg PRN for performance anxiety; 30 - 80 mg/day divided for akathisia
medications.maxCeiling: 80 mg/day (for psychiatric indications; higher for cardiology)
medications.cypMetabolism: Extensively metabolized by CYP2D6, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19.
monitoring: Resting heart rate (hold if HR < 55-60 bpm) and blood pressure
Absolute contraindication: Asthma, severe COPD, or 2nd/3rd degree heart block
medications.clinicalPearls: Lipophilic beta-blocker that readily crosses the blood-brain barrier. Highly effective for somatic symptoms of anxiety (racing heart, sweaty palms, hand tremor, voice quivering) without cognitive dulling or abuse liability. Gold standard first-line antidote for antipsychotic-induced akathisia.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Avoid abrupt cessation in patients with coronary artery disease due to risk of rebound angina or myocardial infarction.

medications.startingDose: 300 mg BID or 600 mg once daily at bedtime (ER formulation)
medications.titration: Titrate by 300 mg every 5-7 days guided by 12-hour trough serum lithium levels
medications.therapeuticRange: Acute Mania: 0.8 - 1.2 mEq/L; Maintenance: 0.6 - 0.8 mEq/L; MDD Augmentation: 0.4 - 0.6 mEq/L
medications.maxCeiling: Do not exceed serum level of 1.2 mEq/L (toxicity emerges at >1.5 mEq/L; lethal >2.0-2.5 mEq/L)
medications.halfLife: 18 - 24 hours (prolonged to >36 hours in elderly or renal impairment)
medications.cypMetabolism: NOT metabolized by CYP450 enzymes; 100% eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.
monitoring: Serum lithium level (drawn exactly 12 hours post-dose as a true trough)
Baseline & every 6-12 mos: BUN, Serum Creatinine, eGFR, TSH/Free T4, urinalysis, electrolytes, and pregnancy test
medications.clinicalPearls: The gold-standard mood stabilizer with robust, proven antisuicidal properties in bipolar disorder and depression. Critical drug interaction rule: NSAIDs (ibuprofen/naproxen), ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and thiazide diuretics dramatically decrease lithium clearance and trigger acute toxicity!
medications.blackBoxWarning: Lithium toxicity is closely related to serum lithium levels and can occur at doses close to therapeutic levels. Facilities for prompt serum lithium determinations must be available.

indications: Bipolar I Disorder Acute Mania & Mixed Episodes
medications.startingDose: Mania: 25 mg/kg/day loading dose or 500 - 750 mg daily in divided doses
medications.titration: Increase by 250 - 500 mg every 2-3 days guided by clinical tolerability and 12-hr trough levels
medications.maxCeiling: 60 mg/kg/day or serum level of 125 mcg/mL
medications.cypMetabolism: Hepatic metabolism via glucuronidation and mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Potent inhibitor of UGT1A4: DOUBLES lamotrigine serum levels!
medications.clinicalPearls: Highly effective for rapid cycling, mixed manic episodes, and comorbid substance use disorders (often superior to lithium in mixed states). Absolute teratogen (causes spina bifida and decreases child IQ by 10 points)—avoid in women of childbearing potential whenever possible.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Hepatic failure resulting in fatalities has occurred, especially in patients with mitochondrial disorders. Severe teratogenicity (neural tube defects). Life-threatening pancreatitis.
